response.reasoning:
Both sides agree on the essentials of what happened: the parcel was sent, tracked, and delivered on 28 August, and the buyer said something was wrong the same day it arrived. Nobody is suggesting a delay or a substitution.

What is really in question is the box condition, and that matters more here than usual because the buyer asked about it directly before buying and was told the boxes were fine and stored in a cupboard since new. The listing says the same thing. So "boxes in good condition" is part of what was sold, not a side detail.

The photographs help more than either party may realise. The outer shipping carton is shown square, sealed and free of any crush, dent or corner damage, with the tape and edges intact. The set box inside it shows a crushed and split top corner and visible wear along the edges. It is hard to see how a corner could be driven in that hard while the carton around it stayed clean and undeformed, so on this evidence the damage more likely came with the item than happened on the way. That points against the description given before purchase, and I do not think the seller is being dishonest so much as judging "fine" more loosely than the buyer did after asking a pointed question.

Against that, the loss is limited. This is four sets for 200. One box is affected, the sets themselves are not said to be incomplete or unusable, and the buyer keeps everything. The right measure is the drop in value caused by one damaged box on a set where packaging carries much of the collector value, plus something for the general wear on a box described as like new. That comes out well short of the whole price and well above nothing.

Twenty per cent of the money being held to the buyer reflects that: a meaningful reduction for the one box that was not as described, with the rest going to the seller for the three sets and the contents that were delivered as promised.

findings.statement: The buyer asked specifically about box condition before buying and was told the boxes were fine and had been stored since new; the listing said the same.
The parcel moved normally and was delivered on 28 August, and the buyer reported the damage the same day.
The outer shipping carton in the buyer's photograph is square, sealed and shows no crush or impact damage.
The set box photographed shows a crushed and split top corner and edge wear, which is difficult to reconcile with an undamaged outer carton and so more likely predates shipping.
The damage is confined to one box out of four sets bought for 200, and there is no claim that any set is incomplete or unusable.
The seller maintains the item was in good condition when sent and was packed carefully, but has provided no photograph of it before posting.
